about: Where the sandbox engine comes from, what it needs on this machine, and `webagents sandbox setup`, the same in both SDKs (the sandbox-engine lane, 2026-09-27). The sandbox is on by default and fails closed, so the engine ships inside both packages: TypeScript depends on srt; Python vendors it (python/scripts/sandbox_engine_vendor.py, webagents/sandbox/sandbox_engine/) and depends on nodejs-wheel-binaries for a node where there is none. Python: webagents/sandbox/srt.py (`locate_srt`, `backend_status`, `setup_checks`), cli/main.py (`sandbox setup`), tests/sandbox/sandbox_engine_setup_test.py and sandbox_engine_bundle_test.py. TypeScript: src/sandbox/srt.ts (`locateSrt`, `backendStatus`, `setupChecks`), src/cli/index.ts, tests/unit/sandbox/sandbox-engine-setup.test.ts. Every string here is what a person or the model sees; both suites assert against it.

order: the engine that ships with webagents

cli_from.bundled: the engine that ships with webagents

engine.version_rule: Exactly the pinned version, whichever wins: srt strips unknown settings keys silently, so another version could drop a rule unseen.

node.python_rule: `node` from PATH when it passes the binary checks and is 20.11 or later, searching the ABSOLUTE PATH entries only (a relative one resolves against the current folder, which a confined command may write); otherwise the node nodejs-wheel-binaries installed, `nodejs_wheel/bin/node` in the folder holding the webagents package or the interpreter's own site-packages (sysconfig, user site), never found through sys.path (which `python -m` starts with the current folder) and never imported. `node --version` runs with an empty environment, so NODE_OPTIONS cannot run code. Nothing is downloaded at run time.
node.typescript_rule: The node running this process (`process.execPath`) or WEBAGENTS_SRT_NODE: the package's own `engines` (>= 22) already covers srt's.

reasons.windows: there is no sandbox on native Windows
reasons.platform: there is no sandbox on {platform}; srt supports macOS and Linux
reasons.programs: {programs} not found in /usr/bin, /bin, /usr/sbin, /sbin, /usr/local/bin; srt needs bubblewrap, socat and ripgrep on Linux
reasons.engine_env_missing: {package}@{version} was not found (WEBAGENTS_SRT_CLI={value} is not a file)
reasons.engine_bundled_missing_python: {package}@{version} is missing from this webagents install ({path} is not a file)
reasons.engine_bundled_missing_typescript: {package}@{version} was not found (it is not installed next to webagents)
reasons.node_env: node was not found for srt (WEBAGENTS_SRT_NODE: {detail})
reasons.node_too_old: {path} is node {found}; srt needs {minimum} or later
reasons.node_unreadable: {path} does not report a node version; srt needs {minimum} or later
reasons.node_missing: no node {minimum} or later for srt ({looked})
reasons.node_looked_path_unreadable: PATH's node does not report a version
reasons.preflight: srt cannot start a sandbox here: {detail}

fixes.windows: run webagents inside WSL 2 (Windows Subsystem for Linux), where the Linux sandbox works
fixes.platform: run webagents on macOS, Linux or WSL 2
fixes.engine_env: point WEBAGENTS_SRT_CLI at srt {version}'s dist/cli.js, or unset it to use the engine that ships with webagents
fixes.node_env: point WEBAGENTS_SRT_NODE at node {minimum} or later, or unset it
fixes.node_missing: reinstall webagents, which brings node through nodejs-wheel-binaries, or install Node {minimum} or later
fixes.tmpdir: point TMPDIR at a short path, such as /tmp/wa: srt's socket path must fit in 104 bytes on macOS
fixes.container: run the container with `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined --security-opt apparmor=unconfined` (or `--privileged`) so bubblewrap can create its namespaces, and as a user other than root
fixes.userns_apparmor: `sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0`, or an AppArmor profile that grants bwrap `userns`

unavailable.about: The refusal when the engine cannot run: the reason, then `: <fix>` when this machine has one, then srt.json's `refusals.unavailable_tail` (the opt-out). `webagents sandbox setup` and `doctor` show the same reason and fix.

example.reason: bwrap, socat not found in /usr/bin, /bin, /usr/sbin, /sbin, /usr/local/bin; srt needs bubblewrap, socat and ripgrep on Linux

install.about: The install line for the Linux programs this machine lacks, from /etc/os-release (`ID`, then each `ID_LIKE` word). Packages are named in the order bwrap, socat, rg.

cases.fix: install bubblewrap socat with your package manager
install ripgrep with your package manager

container.about: Linux only. A container is read from `/.dockerenv`, `/run/.containerenv`, the `container` environment variable, or `/proc/1/cgroup` naming docker, kubepods, containerd, lxc or podman. Said in `sandbox setup` whenever it applies, and as the fix when the confined `true` fails.

namespaces.about: Linux only, read from /proc/sys, in this order; the first that restricts is the fix when the confined `true` fails, and a warning in `sandbox setup` otherwise.

tmpdir.about: macOS only: srt's proxy listens on `join(os.tmpdir(), 'srt-mux-<pid>-<n>.sock')` (its sandbox/mux-proxy.js, started for every run, the preflight's too), and srt's os.tmpdir() is the TMPDIR this SDK gives it, as spelled: the preflight's mkdtemp folder under the temp folder, or a command's scratch folder, which the policy realpaths. macOS's sun_path holds 104 bytes and node uses all of them (measured with real srt: a 104-byte path listened and carried a request, 105 failed with `listen EINVAL`; /Users/vs/webagents-test-artifacts/2026-09-27-ptypass-fixes/06-tmpdir-boundary.txt), so the check measures the longer of the two with the widest pid macOS hands out (5 digits: xnu PID_MAX is 99999) and srt's first socket (`0`), and fails exactly when srt itself would, above 104 bytes (the ptypass-fixes lane, 2026-09-27). The first probe realpath'd the temp folder (a `/private` srt never sees) and counted a 7-digit pid, so every stock Mac read 110 bytes and `sandbox setup` failed while confined commands ran (the PTY pass, 06b, 06d, 07e-tsetup2).

preflight.why: mkdtemp's random suffix is 8 characters in Python and 6 in Node; the temp folder as each runtime spells it, not realpath'd

setup.group_description: The sandbox that confines shell commands
setup.description: Check that the sandbox engine runs on this machine
setup.about: A check, not an installer: it installs nothing and changes nothing. It prints the checks in doctor's layout, runs a real confined `true` through the engine, and exits 1 when commands would be refused. Under --json it is one document, `{checks: [...]}`, as doctor's is.

only_when.namespaces: linux, when one restricts and the confined `true` failed
only_when.install: when webagents, srt or the node srt runs on is installed inside the current folder (a warning; srt.json `sdk_install_deny.report` has the words)

ok.container: inside a container, and bubblewrap works here
ok.confined: a confined `true` ran: shell commands are sandboxed here

fail.namespaces: unprivileged user namespaces are restricted here ({file} is {value})
fail.container: inside a container, where bubblewrap needs namespaces the container may not allow
fail.tmpdir: srt's socket path here is {bytes} bytes ({probe}), over macOS's 104

setup.not_run: not run: fix the checks above first

doctor.about: doctor's `sandbox` line, when the engine cannot run, is `<state>, but <reason>: shell commands are refused`, and its fix is the machine's fix followed by the opt-out.
doctor.fix: {fix}, or pass --no-sandbox to run commands with your permissions for this run
doctor.fix_no_fix: run `webagents sandbox setup` for the details, or pass --no-sandbox to run commands with your permissions for this run
doctor.chat_words: The chat's `/sandbox` fix is `sandboxFix` in cli/chat_edits.json, the same template: `{fix}, or pass --no-sandbox ...`.
